message.content:
Build ONE new file: `/opt/nxeon-wt-kbchat/lib/kb-plans.ts` for the Nxeon platform (Hostinger-style hosting). This is the catalog the AI chat agent uses to render rich "plan cards" (like Hostinger Kodee: a card with badge, price, feature checklist, and a "Get plan" button) inline in chat. The agent only picks card KEYS; the card DATA comes from this file so prices/features are always real.

CONTRACT (match exactly):
```ts
export type PlanCard = {
  key: string;          // stable short id, e.g. "shared-business"
  product: string;      // "Shared hosting" | "VPS" | "Game server" | "Business email"
  name: string;         // "Business"
  badge?: string;       // e.g. "BEST MATCH" | "MOST POPULAR" (optional; leave undefined mostly)
  priceLabel: string;   // "$4.99"
  period: string;       // "/mo"
  oldPriceLabel?: string; // optional slashed price, only if a real promo/discount exists
  features: string[];   // 3-5 short bullet strings, real specs
  ctaLabel: string;     // "Get plan"
  ctaUrl: string;       // real deep link to order/checkout, else the closest real page path
};

export const PLAN_CARDS: Record<string, PlanCard>;      // keyed by PlanCard.key
export function getPlanCards(keys: string[]): PlanCard[]; // lookup, silently drop unknown keys, cap at 3
// A compact human-readable list of the valid keys + one-line descriptions, for the LLM prompt:
export const PLAN_KEYS_FOR_PROMPT: string;
```

STEP 1 — RESEARCH real data (read, don't guess):
- `prisma/seed-hosting-plans.ts` (shared: Starter $2.99, Business $4.99, Pro $8.99 — real storage/site/DB/mailbox counts, which include free migration).
- `prisma/seed.ts` (VPS: Nano $6.49, Starter $8.99, Standard $12.99, Pro $20.99, Max $32.99 — real vCPU/RAM/disk/bandwidth).
- `prisma/seed-gameplans.ts` and `prisma/seed-email-plans.ts` if you want to include a couple of game/email cards (optional — hosting + VPS are the priority).
- Find the REAL order/checkout URLs: grep `app/` for the shared-hosting order flow, VPS order/deploy flow, and the pricing page. Use the most specific real path that starts ordering that product (e.g. something like `/hosting`, `/order`, `/dashboard/...`, or `/pricing`). If you can't find a plan-specific deep link, use the product's order/pricing page path that actually exists. NEVER invent a route — verify it exists under `app/`.

STEP 2 — BUILD the file:
- Cards for ALL shared tiers (`shared-starter`, `shared-business`, `shared-pro`) and ALL VPS tiers (`vps-nano`, `vps-starter`, `vps-standard`, `vps-pro`, `vps-max`). Optionally a few game/email cards (`game-*`, `email-*`) if easy and grounded.
- Features: 3-5 real, short bullets each (e.g. "10 websites", "20 GB NVMe storage", "Free migration", "Free SSL & email", "1-click WordPress").
- `oldPriceLabel` only if there's a real discount to show; otherwise omit (do NOT fabricate a fake "was" price).
- `getPlanCards`: map keys → cards, drop unknowns, cap the result at 3.
- `PLAN_KEYS_FOR_PROMPT`: a compact multi-line string listing each key and a ~6-word description, so the LLM can choose the right ones. Example line: `shared-business — Shared hosting Business $4.99/mo, 10 sites, free migration (best for most WordPress/business sites)`.

Real content only, no placeholders. Touch ONLY `/opt/nxeon-wt-kbchat/lib/kb-plans.ts`. When done, report: the keys you created, the exact ctaUrl used for shared vs VPS (and confirm each route exists under app/), and anything you left out.

Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.

  CARDS.map((c) => [c.key, c]),
);

/**
 * Resolve a list of card keys to their card data.
 * Unknown keys are silently dropped; the result is capped at 3 cards
 * (deduped, order preserved) so a chat message never renders a wall of cards.
 */
export function getPlanCards(keys: string[]): PlanCard[] {
  const out: PlanCard[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  for (const key of keys) {
    if (seen.has(key)) continue;
    const card = PLAN_CARDS[key];
    if (!card) continue;
    seen.add(key);
    out.push(card);
    if (out.length >= 3) break;
  }
  return out;
}
